Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year was Scurvy discovered?
Scurvy or scorbutus is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
In what year was Polonium discovered?
Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
Spironolactone: Pfizer. Spironolactone, sold under the brand name Aldactone among others, is classed as a diuretic medication.
In which country did the Chengdu J-10 take place?

Chengdu J-10: People's Republic of China. It is produced by the Chengdu Aircraft Corporation (CAC) for the People's Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) of China, and exported to the Pakistan Air Force (PAF).
Who is credited with discovering Seaborgium?
Seaborgium: Yuri Oganessian. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen cyanide?
Hydrogen cyanide: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula H−C≡N.
Who is credited with discovering Tungsten?
Tungsten: Juan José Elhuyar. Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
This genus of succulent, spiky-leaved plants native to the arid Americas typically takes years to mature, with each rosette flowering only once before dying — what's the genus called?
Agave (Anglo-Hispanic) is a genus of monocots native to the arid regions of the Americas.
In 1978, a run-in with a particle accelerator's proton beam left this Russian physicist with an extraordinary survival story after it passed straight through his head — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski (born 25 June 1942) is a Russian retired particle physicist.
This red giant is the brightest star in the constellation Boötes and the fourth-brightest star in the entire night sky — name the star?
Arcturus is a red giant star in the northern constellation of Botes, and the brightest star in the constellation.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, members of this order — the second largest among mammals — fly using long digits webbed by a thin membrane. What are they?
Bat (order Chiroptera) are winged mammals, the only mammals capable of true and sustained flight.
Native to cool parts of Europe and Asia, this deciduous shrub produces small, glossy black berries especially rich in vitamin C and vulnerable to cold snaps during spring flowering — name the fruit?
Blackcurrant (Ribes nigrum), black currant or cassis is a deciduous shrub in the family Grossulariaceae grown for its edible berries.
Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide and often striking during sleep, this parafunctional habit grinds teeth and clenches jaws until enamel wears away — what's it called?
Bruxism is excessive teeth grinding or jaw clenching.

Which German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist discovered oxygen — though Priestley published first — and identified elements like molybdenum, tungsten, and chlorine before reportedly dying of mercury poisoning?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele (9 December 1742 - 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.

Sold under the brand name Thorazine, this phenothiazine antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder — but it's also been used for nausea, pre-surgery anxiety, and even stubborn hiccups. What is it?
Chlorpromazine (CPZ), marketed under the brand names Thorazine and Largactil among others, is an antipsychotic medication.
Native to Asia but so invasive in Australian cities that it was dubbed 'Most Important Pest/Problem' in 2008, which urban-adapted bird species is this?
Common myna (Acridotheres tristis), sometimes spelled mynah, is a bird in the family Sturnidae, native to Asia.
This bluish-purple discoloration of the skin, most visible on the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes, signals a drop in oxygen bound to hemoglobin in the blood — name the condition?
Cyanosis is the change of tissue color to a bluish-purple hue, as a result of decrease in the amount of oxygen bound to the hemoglobin in the red blood cells of the capillary bed.
Bred around 1890 in Thuringia by a tax collector seeking a loyal protector, this German working-dog breed is known in North America by a slightly different two-word name — which breed?
Dobermann is a German breed of medium-large working dog of pinscher type.

This German chess champion — also a mathematician and philosopher — held the world title for 27 years, the longest reign ever, and was famed for a 'psychological' approach said to unsettle opponents. Who was he?
Emanuel Lasker (German; December 24, 1868 - January 11, 1941) was a German chess player, mathematician, and philosopher.

This front-of-the-head feature found in humans and other animals houses most of the sense organs, including the eyes, nose, and mouth, and its damage can profoundly affect one's sense of identity — name this body part?
Face is the front of the head in humans and many other animals that features most of the sense organs including the eyes, nose and mouth.
Having led Renault, Sauber, and Alfa Romeo's F1 outfits, this French engineer took the reins at Ferrari as team principal in 2023 — who is he?
Fred Vasseur (French; born 28 May 1968) is a French motorsport executive, businessman and engineer.

Colorless, odorless, and oddly sweet, this viscous sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of every triglyceride in animal fat, and moonlights as a food sweetener — what is it?
Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Hailed by Time as a 2019 'Pioneer' yet condemned as a mad scientist, which Chinese biophysicist announced in 2018 that he'd created the first gene-edited human babies?
He Jiankui (pinyin: H Jinku HUH KWAY; born 1984) is a Chinese biophysicist known for his controversial first use of genome editing in humans in 2018.
While first described from Virginia, this genus of flowering shrubs reaches its greatest diversity in East Asia, and some species climb up to 30 metres by scaling trees. What plant is it?
Hydrangea (or) is a genus of more than 70 species of flowering plants native to Asia and the Americas.
These creatures don't breathe through a nose or lungs — air enters through tiny paired openings along their sides, piped straight to the tissues. What hexapod group are they?
Insect (from Latin insectum) are hexapod invertebrates of the class Insecta.
This financier's 1999 bestseller on mutual funds became an investment classic after he founded a low-cost investing giant — who is he?

John C. Bogle (May 8, 1929 - January 16, 2019) was an American investor, business magnate and philanthropist who was the founder of The Vanguard Group and is credited with popularizing the index fund.
Alongside Robert Goddard and Hermann Oberth, this reclusive Russian scientist who lived in a log house near Kaluga is considered a founding father of modern rocketry — who is he?

This scientific discipline studies language through areas like syntax, semantics, morphology, and phonology, with subfields examining its biological roots and psychological underpinnings — name the field?
Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguistics encompasses many branches and subfields that span both theoretical and practical applications.

With degrees from Stanford in chemical engineering and a medical degree from Cornell, this physician-astronaut spent nearly eight days aboard Endeavour in 1992, becoming the first African-American woman in space — who is she?
Mae Jemison (born October 17, 1956) is an American engineer, physician, and former NASA astronaut.
Most common on the legs in women and the back in men, this cancer develops from melanin-producing skin cells and, in extremely rare cases, can even arise in the lungs — which cancer?
Melanoma is a type of cancer, typically skin cancer; it develops from the melanin-producing cells known as melanocytes.
These cylindrical, burrowing insects have small eyes and shovel-like front limbs highly adapted for digging underground — name the family?
Mole cricket are members of the insect family Gryllotalpidae, in the order Orthoptera (grasshoppers, locusts, and crickets).
This flexible body part lets the head turn in every direction while its compartments guard the spinal cord and upper airway between head and torso — what is it, also known as the cervix?
Neck is the part of the body in many vertebrates that connects the head to the torso.
Named after a German physicist, this SI unit of electrical resistance is represented by the uppercase Greek letter omega — name the unit?
Ohm (symbol:, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).

This skin sensation — often described as tingling, prickling, or numbness — is most familiar as the 'pins and needles' feeling after a limb falls asleep from staying still too long — name this sensation?
Paresthesia (or paraesthesia) is a sensation of the skin that may feel like numbness (hypoesthesia), tingling, pricking, chilling, or burning.
Colorless in acid and a vivid pink in base, which phthalein dye is the chemist's go-to indicator for acid-base titrations?
Phenolphthalein (feh-NOL(F)-th-leen) is a chemical compound with the formula C20H14O4 and is often written as "HIn", "HPh", "phph" or simply "Ph" in shorthand notation.

This academic field studies systems of governance and power, favoring descriptive and empirical analysis of behavior and institutions over the value judgments used in philosophy about the state — name the discipline?
Political science (sometimes abbreviated as poli sci) is a field which aims to study the scientific aspect of politics.

This medical specialty diagnoses, treats, and prevents disorders of cognition, perception, mood, emotion, and behavior, typically beginning assessment with a case history and mental status exam — name the field?
Psychiatry is the medical specialty devoted to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of deleterious mental conditions.
One of the three ancient arts of discourse alongside grammar and logic, this discipline studies the techniques speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate an audience — what is it?
Rhetoric is the art of persuasion.
Which plant genus in the mint family, comprising nearly 1,000 species of shrubs and perennials, includes both a common cooking herb and — surprisingly — rosemary as one of its species?
Salvia is the largest genus of plants in the sage family Lamiaceae, with just under 1,000 species of shrubs, herbaceous perennials, and annuals.

Though many are crustaceans more closely related to insects than to fish, which group of exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates, including molluscs and echinoderms, is a leading cause of food allergies?
Shellfish are exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates used as food, including various species of molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms.

Extending from the base of the brainstem down to the lower back, this tubular bundle of nervous tissue is covered by the meninges and, together with the brain, makes up the central nervous system — name this structure?

Spinal cord is a long, thin, tubular structure made up of nervous tissue that extends from the medulla oblongata in the lower brainstem to the lumbar region of the vertebral column (backbone) of vertebrate animals.
Also called 'true comfrey,' this Boraginaceae perennial is native to damp European meadows and popular with bumblebees, despite carrying warnings about liver toxicity if eaten — which plant?
Symphytum officinale is a perennial flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
This condition causes abnormally low platelet levels in the blood, leading to prolonged or excessive bleeding — what blood disorder is it?
Thrombocytopenia is a condition characterized by abnormally low levels of platelets (also known as thrombocytes) in the blood.
The most widespread New World scavenger of its kind, this bird sniffs out the gases of early decay to find carrion and rides thermals instead of flapping — which bird?
Turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) is the most widespread of the New World vultures.

Its small molecule packs a surprising punch: strong polarity, relentless hydrogen bonding, and a starring role as the fluid of all known life and the main stuff of Earth's oceans — what compound is it?
Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O.

Released from prison in June 2025 to resume leading Turkey's nationalist Victory Party, this politician previously served as deputy leader of the far-right Nationalist Movement Party in the mid-2010s — who is he?
Ümit Özdağ (born 3 March 1961) is a Turkish politician who returned to his position as the current leader of the Victory Party after being released from prison on 17 June 2025.
Recognizable by its black-and-white striped legs and a lyre-shaped marking on its thorax, this mosquito native to North Africa spreads dengue and yellow fever worldwide — what is it?
Aedes aegypti: Species of mosquito. The mosquito can be recognized by black and white markings on its legs and a marking in the form of a lyre on the upper surface of its thorax.
This diverse group of photosynthetic organisms ranges from microscopic plankton to seaweeds 50 metres long — yet excludes the land plants entirely. What is it?
Algae: Diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. Algae (AL-jee, UK also AL-ghee; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
Unlike fear, which responds to a threat that's already here, this emotional state involves dread over something that hasn't happened yet, often paired with pacing and rumination. What is it?
About 200 times sweeter than table sugar, this artificial sweetener sold as NutraSweet and Equal had its FDA approval briefly revoked before being re-approved in 1981 — what is it?
Named from a Greek word meaning 'heavy,' this soft silvery alkaline earth metal with atomic number 56 wasn't isolated until 1808 via electrolysis, decades after being identified — which element?
Barium: Chemical element with atomic number 56 (Ba)
Also called the bearcat, this dark, shaggy, tree-dwelling Asian viverrid sports a prehensile tail and musk glands that famously smell of buttered popcorn — what is it?
Binturong: Asian mammal also known as a bearcat.
Built as a militarized derivative of a popular 737 airliner, this maritime patrol aircraft hunts submarines for the US Navy and allies like India, Australia and the UK — which aircraft?
Boeing P-8 Poseidon: American maritime patrol aircraft. The Boeing P-8 Poseidon is an American maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft developed and produced by Boeing Defense, Space & Security.

Characterized by cycles of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like self-induced vomiting, this eating disorder has an estimated genetic risk factor between 30 and 80 percent — what is it called?
Bulimia nervosa: Eating disorder. Bulimia is more common among those who have a close relative with the condition.
Discovered in 1940 and making up as much as 40% of cannabis extract, this compound is an anticonvulsant used to treat two rare forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?

Cannabidiol: Phytocannabinoid discovered in 1940. In the United States, the cannabidiol drug Epidiolex was approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2018, for the treatment of two seizure disorders.
Their young are calves and their castrated males are oxen; this widespread bovid is the most far-flung species of the genus Bos — what animal is it?
Its roasted root has long served as a coffee substitute, while today its extracted inulin shows up as a sweetener and fiber additive in packaged foods — which blue-flowered plant?
Chicory: Flowering plant in the daisy family.
Sold under the brand name Plavix, this antiplatelet drug taken after a heart attack or coronary stent placement kicks in within two hours and keeps working for five days — what is it?

Clopidogrel: Antiplatelet medication. Clopidogrel, sold under the brand name Plavix among others, is an antiplatelet medication used to reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke in those at high risk.
This towering annual in the daisy family yields the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil, plus snackable seeds and birdseed — and its wild cousins sprout multiple flower heads. What is it?
Common sunflower: Species of flowering plant in the family of Asteraceae.
This genus of some 100 low-growing perennials gives us saffron from the dried stigmas of one autumn-blooming species — name the flower genus?
Introduced in 1984, this turboprop regional airliner series was developed from an earlier company model and later gained 'Quiet' variants with active noise-cancellation — which aircraft family?

De Havilland Canada Dash 8: Canadian turboprop airliner. The De Havilland Canada DHC-8, commonly known as the Dash 8, is a series of turboprop-powered regional airliners, introduced by de Havilland Canada (DHC) in 1984.

The largest collection of fossils from this extinct Ice Age canine came from the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, though it roamed from South American savanna to North American forested mountains — what animal was it?
Dire wolf: Extinct species of canine mammal.
Its name comes from the Greek word for 'house,' and it studies organisms from the level of a single individual all the way up to the entire biosphere — which branch of biology is it?
Ecology: Study of organisms and their environment.
In this concept, a random variable's average uncertainty is measured by how much data is needed, on average, to describe which outcome occurred. What is this quantity called?

Entropy (information theory): Average uncertainty in variable's states. The choice of base for

 {\displaystyle \log }, the logarithm, varies for different applications.
With a cinnamon body, black-and-white wings, and a tall erectile crest, this widespread bird announces itself with a soft 'oop-oop-oop' call — what is it?
Eurasian hoopoe: Species of bird. The Eurasian hoopoe or common hoopoe (Upupa epops) is the most widespread species of hoopoe.
This number-theory rule holds that if p is prime, then for any integer a, the value a to the power p minus a is always a multiple of p — which rule is this?

Fermat's little theorem: A prime p divides a^p–a for any integer a. Fermat's little theorem is the basis for the Fermat primality test and is one of the fundamental results of elementary number theory.
Called the "father of modern parasitology," this Italian physician-poet famously dismantled spontaneous generation by showing that maggots hatch from fly eggs — who was he?
Francesco Redi: Italian naturalist and poet. Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 – 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.

Named after a long-nosed, insect-eating African animal, this 1960s supersonic fighter-bomber pioneered variable-sweep wings and automated terrain-following radar under Robert McNamara's TFX program. What aircraft is it?
General Dynamics F-111 Aardvark: Family of strike aircraft developed in 1960s.
Dubbed the 'king of the birds' in European folklore for its golden head crest, this tiny kinglet's scientific name literally means 'petty king' — which bird?
Goldcrest: Small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Combined with obstetrics as a joint medical specialty and touching on everything from family planning to pelvic reconstructive surgery, which field focuses on the female reproductive system?
Gynaecology: Medical area for women's reproductive health.

This French mathematician, famous for his work in algebraic topology, came from an almost absurdly mathematical dynasty: son of mathematician Élie, nephew of mathematician Anna, and brother to a composer, a physicist, and yet another mathematician — who was he?
This small rodent, pointed-snouted with large rounded ears, has become the standard laboratory model organism after thriving alongside human settlements — what is it?
Once down to just 94 individuals in Andalusia by 2002, largely due to a crash in its rabbit prey from myxomatosis, this medium-sized wild cat is endemic to a European peninsula — which species?
Iberian lynx: Species of mammal. The Iberian lynx (Lynx pardinus) is one of four extant species of Lynx, a genus of medium-sized wild cats.
This 12th-century polymath from Mesopotamia wrote a treatise describing 50 ingenious mechanical devices, including his famous elephant clock, earning him the title 'father of robotics' — who is he?
Ismail al-Jazari: Muslim engineer and artist (1136–1206)
Once an assistant to astronomer Tycho Brahe and later imperial mathematician to Emperor Rudolf II, this polymath formulated the laws of planetary motion — who was he?
Johannes Kepler: German astronomer and mathematician (1571–1630)
Nicknamed 'The Professor' on The Chase, this record-breaking contestant won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004 before eventually becoming its host — who is he?
Ken Jennings: American game show host (born 1974)
Known by common names like true lavender and English lavender despite not being native to England, this Mediterranean-basin plant belongs to the mint family — which species?
Lavandula angustifolia: Species of plant. Lavandula angustifolia, formerly L. officinalis, is a flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to the Mediterranean basin.
A sweet, aromatic flavouring used in confectionery, tobacco, and pharmaceuticals comes from the root of which legume — though more than a couple of milligrams per kilo a day can cause trouble?
Painlessly swollen lymph nodes, drenching night sweats, and unexplained weight loss point to this family of white-blood-cell cancers, split mainly into Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin types — what is it?
Lymphoma: Hematologic cancer that affects lymphocytes.
The second woman ever to win the Nobel Prize in Physics (after Marie Curie) shared the 1963 award for her discoveries about nuclear shell structure — who was she?
Also called pennyroyal, this minty flowering plant native to Europe, North Africa and the Middle East has a folk-remedy history despite being toxic to the liver — what species is it?
Soviet pilots nicknamed this 1972 gunship the 'flying tank,' a helicopter NATO calls 'Hind' that can also haul eight troops and still flies in 52 countries. What is it?
Mil Mi-24: Family of assault and attack helicopters.
Forming dense green mats with leaves just one cell thick, these seedless plants reproduce via spore-topped stalks called sporophytes — which plants?
Moss: Division of typically non-vascular land plants.
The sole surviving family of an ancient cephalopod lineage, these nine living species carry coiled chambered shells 10 to 25 cm across and are all protected under CITES — what creatures are they?
Nautilus: Family of molluscs. It comprises nine living species in two genera, the type of which is the genus Nautilus.

As the United States' first swept-wing fighter jet, this Korean War-era aircraft dueled Soviet MiG-15s in some of history's earliest jet-to-jet battles — which plane, produced in more than 7,800 units?
North American F-86 Sabre: Family of US fighter aircraft.
The most arboreal of the great apes, with long arms, short legs and reddish-brown hair, this genus Pongo primate survives today only in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra — what is it?
Orangutan: Genus of Asian apes. The most arboreal of the great apes, orangutans spend most of their time in trees.

Named for its resemblance to a related crested dinosaur, this duck-billed herbivore could grow over 9 meters long, moved on two or four legs, and was first described in 1922 by William Parks — which dinosaur genus?
Parasaurolophus: Hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur genus from Late Cretaceous Period.
Created by Larry Wall in 1987 as a Unix scripting tool for report processing, this language's planned sixth version was eventually spun off and renamed Raku — which programming language?
Perl: Interpreted programming language first released in 1987.
Manufactured in Switzerland since 1991, this pressurized single-engine turboprop's large aft cargo door has made it popular with air-ambulance operators and police departments alike — which aircraft?
Pilatus PC-12: Swiss executive and utility transport aircraft.
Emerging in the 1960s as scholars from once-colonized nations began writing back, this academic field examines the lingering cultural and political effects of empire — what's it called?
Postcolonialism: Study of the cultural legacy of colonialism and imperialism.
This emotional response to severe distressing events like violence or a life-threatening injury can trigger flashbacks, panic attacks, insomnia, and post-traumatic stress disorder — what's it called?
Psychological trauma: Emotional response caused by severe distressing events.
This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species includes the buttercups, spearworts, and water crowfoots — which genus?
Ranunculus: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family.
Its seeds yield castor oil but also harbor a highly potent toxin — which plant genus, better known for producing the castor bean?
Ricinus: Monotypic genus of plant in the spurge family.
Sold under the brand name Ventolin, this fast-acting inhaled medication opens the airways within about 15 minutes to treat asthma attacks and COPD — what is it?
Salbutamol: Short-acting bronchodilator used for acute asthma.
This long-term skin condition causes flaky, greasy patches on the scalp, face, and chest, and is called cradle cap when it appears on a baby's scalp — what is it?
Seborrhoeic dermatitis: Skin disease. Seborrhoeic dermatitis (also spelled seborrheic dermatitis in American English) is a long-term skin disorder.
The brightest star in Earth's night sky, this binary system in Canis Major pairs a bright main-sequence star with a faint white dwarf companion — which star?
Sirius: Brightest star in Earth's night sky. Its name is derived from the Greek word Σείριος (Latin script: Seirios; lit. 'glowing' or 'scorching').
Native to Central and Western Asia, this leafy green vegetable's high oxalate content can be reduced by blanching before eating — what is it?
Made by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and roughly 600 times sweeter than it, what is this sugar substitute also known by the E number E955?
This daisy-family weed's yellow flowers give way to fluffy silver-tufted seed heads nicknamed 'clocks' or 'blowballs,' whose seeds scatter on the wind — which plant, better known by its common name?
Taraxacum officinale: Flowering plant species known as dandelion.
This French aerospace engineer flew to the International Space Station twice, first as a 2016 European Space Agency flight engineer and again in 2021 aboard a SpaceX Crew Dragon — who is he?
Thomas Pesquet: French aerospace engineer, pilot, and astronaut.
Inside a ribosome, this cellular process reads messenger RNA three nucleotides at a time to build a chain of amino acids into protein — what is it called?
Translation (biology): Cellular process of protein synthesis. Translation is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.
RIKEN has been trying to synthesize this hypothetical element 119 since 2018 — the lightest element not yet made and the first of the eighth period. What is it?
Ununennium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 119 (Uue)
Also known scientifically as emesis, this forceful bodily reflex expels stomach contents through the mouth—and sometimes the nose—often preceded by a queasy feeling called nausea. What is it?
Vomiting: Expulsion of stomach contents via the mouth or nose.
Famous for drumming tree trunks with its beak to forage for insects and send signals, one desert species of this bird family pecks into cacti instead — what is it?
Woodpecker: Family of birds. The family Picidae includes about 240 species arranged in 35 genera.
Yttrium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for yttrium is Y. Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
Germanium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for germanium is Ge. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.

Helen McCrory: Helen Elizabeth McCrory (17 August 1968 – 16 April 2021) was an English actress.
